Stealth attacks can maximize state estimation error without triggering alarms, causing systems to deviate into critical states.
Existing detectors are vulnerable to stealth attacks designed with system knowledge to avoid detection.
The paper defines the ASR set as the set of states reachable by an attacker stealthily during an attack time interval.
The system model is a nonlinear discrete-time system with process noise and measurement noise.
State estimation is performed using the Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF).
A chi-square detector on residuals is used to detect attacks, with stealth attacks constrained to keep residuals within a tolerance region.
Attackers are assumed to have complete system knowledge and unlimited computational resources.
Zonotopes are used for set representation due to computational efficiency in reachability analysis.
Taylor models are used to approximate nonlinear functions and over-approximate ellipsoids.
The paper proposes the Stealth Reachability Analysis (SRA) algorithm to approximate the ASR set for nonlinear systems.
The risk field concept formalizes scenario risk distribution by combining critical regions and loss expectations.
The Reachability and Risk field-based (RR) metric dynamically quantifies risk by checking intersections between ASR sets and risk sets.
Noise regions are bounded using chi-square thresholds to handle infinite reachability due to randomness.
The framework provides early warnings for safety control by predicting risk values dynamically.
The case study involves an automated warehouse scenario to demonstrate the framework's effectiveness.
The framework integrates system dynamics, noise, attack stealthiness, and scenario risks in risk assessment.
The paper uses Lipschitz continuity assumptions for system and controller functions.
The Minkowski sum operation is used to combine sets in reachability computations.
The framework does not require knowledge of specific attacker strategies but analyzes the region of stealthy residuals.
The paper extends reachability analysis from linear to nonlinear systems under stealth attacks.
